header.title: Divina Bibliotheca 02. Liber Elle Smoth Qui Dicitur Exodus: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Jerome, Saint
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tmp497.tmp497.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

The bracketed chapter numbers and the notes '[Vulg. add. ipse]' and '[h. Eterit, si clamaverit]' belong to the edition and are kept; the second '[C. LVIII.]' is evidently a misprint for LXVIII, and 'h.' is unexplained. 'The gods' (deos, deis) renders the Latin as it stands; the sense 'judges' is often given to these places. 'occisura' is read as 'occisum' and a stray 'a' is ignored.

nodes.text: [C. LV, Ch. XXII] If anyone steals an ox or a sheep, and kills or sells it, he shall restore five oxen for one ox, and four sheep for one sheep. [C. LVI.] If a thief is found breaking into a house or digging under it, and is wounded and dies, the one who struck him shall not be guilty of blood. But if he did this after the sun had risen, he has committed homicide, and he himself shall die. If [the thief] has nothing to repay for the theft, [Vulg. adds: he himself] he shall be sold. If what he stole is found with him alive, whether ox or ass or sheep, he shall restore double. [C. LVII.] If anyone damages a field or a vineyard, and lets his beast loose to graze on what belongs to another, he shall restore, according to the estimate of the damage, whatever is best in his own field or vineyard. [C. LVIII.] If a fire breaks out and catches thorns, and seizes stacks of grain or crops standing in the fields, the one who lit the fire shall make good the loss. [C. LIX.] If anyone entrusts money or a vessel to a friend for safekeeping, and they are stolen from the one who received them: if the thief is found, he shall repay double. If the thief is not found, the master of the house shall be brought before the gods, and shall swear that he did not stretch out his hand to his neighbour's property to commit fraud, whether in ox or ass or sheep or garment; and whatever loss can be caused, the case of both shall come before the gods, and if they give judgement, he shall restore double to his neighbour. [C. LX.] If anyone entrusts to his neighbour an ass, an ox, a sheep or any beast for safekeeping, and it dies, or is injured, or is captured by enemies, and no one saw this, there shall be an oath between them that he did not stretch out his hand to his neighbour's property; and the owner shall accept the oath, and the other shall not be compelled to make restitution. But if it was stolen, he shall make good the loss to the owner. If it was eaten by a wild beast, let him bring him what was killed, and he shall not make restitution. [C. LXI.] Whoever asks his neighbour for the loan of any of these, and it is injured or dies when the owner is not present, shall be compelled to make restitution. But if the owner was present, he shall not make restitution, especially if it had come hired for the price of its work. [C. LXII.] If anyone seduces a virgin not yet betrothed and sleeps with her, he shall give her a dowry and have her as his wife. If the virgin's father is unwilling to give her, he shall pay money according to the measure of the dowry that virgins are accustomed to receive. [C. LXIII.] You shall not allow sorcerers to live. [C. LXIV.] Whoever has intercourse with a beast, let him be put to death. [C. LXV.] Whoever sacrifices to gods, except to the Lord alone, shall be killed. [C. LXVI.] You shall not grieve a stranger, nor afflict him: for you yourselves were also strangers in the land of Egypt. [C. LXVII.] You shall not harm a widow or an orphan. If you hurt them, they will cry out to me, and I will hear their cry, and my fury will be roused, and I will strike you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows and your children orphans. [C. LVIII.] If you lend money to my people, to the poor man who lives among you, you shall not press him like a debt-collector, nor crush him with interest. If you take your neighbour's garment as a pledge, you shall return it to him before sunset. For that is his only covering, the clothing of his flesh, and he has nothing else to sleep in; if he cries [h.: and it shall be, if he cries] to me, I will hear him, because I am merciful. [C. LXIX.] You shall not disparage the gods, and you shall not curse the ruler of your people. [C. LXX.] You shall not delay to offer your tithes and your first-fruits. [C. LXXI.] You shall give me the firstborn of your sons. You shall do likewise with oxen and sheep: let it be seven days with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it back to me. [C. LXXII.] You shall be holy men to me. You shall not eat flesh that has first been tasted by wild beasts, but you shall throw it to the dogs.
